editor_note: None of the 10 rewritten entries changes the meaning. The permission table (59) keeps every ✅/❌/✴️ and every qualifier, and the roles table (63) keeps every role-to-action mapping. The service name is inconsistent: entries 10, 12 and 38 keep "IBM Quantum Compute Service" in English, but entry 59 gives "Perkhidmatan IBM Quantum Compute", and "Premium Plan" comes out as a half-translated "Plan Premium". Entry 59 also uses "ke" where Malay needs "kepada" (e.g. "Hanya ke instans Quantum Compute"). Entry 54 translates the literal auto-generated group name "Collaborators" as "Rakan usaha sama", which users won't find on screen.

examples.source: (*Only to IBM Quantum Compute Service*)
examples.translation: (*Hanya ke Perkhidmatan IBM Quantum Compute*)
examples.suggested: (*Hanya kepada IBM Quantum Compute Service*)
examples.why: Entries 10, 12 and 38 keep the product name 'IBM Quantum Compute Service' in English; here it is partly translated. 'ke' is for places and directions, so non-physical access takes 'kepada'.

examples.source: (*If the access group gives access to a Premium Plan instance*)
examples.translation: (*Jika kumpulan akses memberi akses ke instans Plan Premium*)
examples.suggested: (*Jika kumpulan akses memberi akses kepada instans Premium Plan*)
examples.why: 'Plan Premium' is neither the English product name nor proper Malay ('Pelan Premium'), so the plan name is hard to recognise.

examples.source: a "Collaborators" access group is automatically generated
examples.translation: kumpulan akses "Rakan usaha sama" dijana secara automatik
examples.suggested: kumpulan akses "Collaborators" (rakan usaha sama) dijana secara automatik
examples.why: The quotes mark the literal name of the auto-generated group. A translated name won't match what users see in the console.

examples.source: See instance usage and remaining time
examples.translation: Lihat penggunaan instans dan masa yang tinggal
examples.suggested: Lihat penggunaan instans dan baki masa
examples.why: 'baki masa' is the idiomatic Malay term for remaining time or quota; 'masa yang tinggal' reads as a literal calque.

editor_note: The translation is faithful and I found nothing that would mislead a learner. The caveat in [20] about noise drift and the claim in [15] that no method can do better on overhead are both kept intact. The worst problem is in [17]: IC-POVM is garbled as "ukuran operator bernilai pengendali positif", which inserts an extra "operator" and puts "pengendali" (a 'handler') where "operator" belongs. [27] also uses "pengendali" for the operator, so the term is inconsistent within the file. There are smaller stiff spots: [11] reads as if the observables are what mitigate the errors, [15] has the redundant "masa runtime" and the awkward "selepas jalankan kalibrasi", and [30] uses "meniru isu" for 'reproduce the issue'.

examples.line_approx: Circuit diukur dengan ukuran operator bernilai pengendali positif
examples.source: informationally complete positive operator-valued measure (IC-POVM)
examples.translation: ukuran operator bernilai pengendali positif yang lengkap maklumat (IC-POVM)
examples.suggested: ukuran bernilai operator positif yang lengkap maklumat (IC-POVM)
examples.why: This is the name of a technical term, but it is garbled. 'Operator' appears twice, and one of them is the non-mathematical word 'pengendali' ('handler').

examples.source: for the given operator
examples.translation: bagi pengendali yang diberikan
examples.suggested: bagi operator yang diberikan
examples.why: 'Pengendali' means a handler or operator in the everyday sense. The mathematical operator is conventionally called 'operator', which is the word [17] also uses.

examples.line_approx: nilai jangkaan observables yang mengurangkan ralat
examples.source: compute the expectation values of observables mitigating the inevitable noise-induced errors
examples.translation: mengira nilai jangkaan observables yang mengurangkan ralat yang disebabkan oleh hingar
examples.suggested: mengira nilai jangkaan observables sambil memitigasi ralat akibat hingar yang tidak dapat dielakkan
examples.why: The relative clause 'yang mengurangkan' attaches to 'observables', so it sounds as if the observables do the mitigating. Using an adverbial clause makes it clear that the mitigation happens during the computation.

examples.source: after a short calibration run
examples.translation: selepas jalankan kalibrasi yang singkat
examples.suggested: selepas larian kalibrasi yang singkat
examples.why: 'Jalankan' is a bare verb used where a noun is needed, which is ungrammatical here. In the same list item, 'masa runtime' is redundant.

examples.source: Steps to reproduce the issue
examples.translation: Langkah untuk meniru isu
examples.suggested: Langkah untuk menghasilkan semula isu
examples.why: 'Meniru' means 'imitate'. For reproducing a bug, the conventional wording is 'menghasilkan semula'.

editor_note: The meaning is accurate throughout. The beta caveat and the "qiskit-ibm-runtime 0.47.0 atau lebih tinggi" requirement are kept, and so is the "first previewed at QDC 2025" detail. One word should change: in entry [7], "error suppression" is translated as "penindasan ralat". "Penindasan" usually means oppression, so a native technical editor would write "penyekatan ralat". Everything else reads naturally, e.g. "model pelaksanaan terarah" and "pembelajaran hingar".

examples.source: several built-in error mitigation and suppression techniques
examples.translation: beberapa teknik mitigasi dan penindasan ralat terbina dalam
examples.suggested: beberapa teknik mitigasi dan penyekatan ralat terbina dalam
examples.why: 'Penindasan' means oppression and reads as a literal dictionary pick. 'Penyekatan' is the natural technical word for suppressing errors.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout and nothing would mislead a learner. The adder example (A=2, B=3, 5 in all 1024 shots), the data-encoding caveats and the claims about quantum volume all match the English. The problems are phrasing, mostly in entry [34]. 'post-processing results' became the awkward 'memproses keputusan pasca'. 'instruction fidelity' became 'kesetiaan arahan', and 'kesetiaan' reads as loyalty rather than technical fidelity. 'reliably run' became the clumsy 'dijalankan dengan boleh percaya'. Separately, the heading in [9] starts with a lowercase letter ('gate piawai'), and 'unitary' was left in English in [29] ('kluster berganding unitary').

examples.source: the software stack transpiling and post-processing results
examples.translation: tumpukan perisian yang mentranspil dan memproses keputusan pasca
examples.suggested: tumpukan perisian yang melakukan transpilasi dan pasca-pemprosesan keputusan
examples.why: 'memproses keputusan pasca' is a calque with the word order garbled. Malay uses 'pasca-pemprosesan' as the noun.

examples.source: instruction fidelity ... the size of the circuit it can reliably run
examples.translation: kesetiaan arahan ... saiz Circuit yang boleh dijalankan dengan boleh percaya
examples.suggested: kefidelan arahan ... saiz Circuit yang boleh dijalankan secara boleh dipercayai
examples.why: 'kesetiaan' means loyalty, not technical fidelity. 'dengan boleh percaya' is ungrammatical and stiff.

examples.source: Standard gates
examples.translation: gate piawai
examples.suggested: Gate piawai
examples.why: The heading starts with a lowercase letter, unlike every other heading on the page.

examples.source: unitary coupled-cluster trial states
examples.translation: keadaan percubaan kluster berganding unitary
examples.suggested: keadaan percubaan kluster berganding unitari
examples.why: 'unitary' was left in English inside an otherwise Malay phrase. The Malay form is 'unitari'.

editor_note: The two rewritten tables keep their meaning: the role permissions, the "beyond the reader/writer role" chain, cost limit, and delete/cancel all match. Three things are inconsistent with the rest of the page. The service name "Quantum Compute" is translated as "Pengkomputeran Kuantum" in both table headers, but entries 17, 22 and 27 keep "Quantum Compute", which is the label the learner has to pick from the IAM dropdown. "jobs" becomes "tugas" in entry 25, while the prose uses "kerja" throughout ("menjalankan kerja", "memadam kerja"). Also, "provisioning instances" is rendered as the bare noun "peruntukan instans" in a list of verb phrases, where "memperuntukkan instans" would keep the parallel structure.

examples.source: | Platform management role | Quantum Compute |
examples.translation: | Peranan pengurusan platform | Pengkomputeran Kuantum |
examples.suggested: | Peranan pengurusan platform | Quantum Compute |
examples.why: Quantum Compute is the IBM Cloud service name that users select in the dropdown, and the rest of the page (entries 17, 22, 27) keeps it in English. Translating it only here is inconsistent and does not match the UI.

examples.source: Perform read-only actions, such as viewing jobs ... including running jobs ... deleting or canceling a job
examples.translation: seperti melihat tugas ... termasuk menjalankan tugas ... memadam atau membatalkan tugas
examples.suggested: seperti melihat kerja ... termasuk menjalankan kerja ... memadam atau membatalkan kerja
examples.why: The page's prose renders 'job' as 'kerja' (entries 11, 18, 20, 22), so switching to 'tugas' in the table splits the term.

examples.source: including provisioning instances, setting the instance cost limit, and deleting or canceling a job
examples.translation: termasuk peruntukan instans, menetapkan had kos instans, dan memadam atau membatalkan tugas
examples.suggested: termasuk memperuntukkan instans, menetapkan had kos instans, dan memadam atau membatalkan kerja
examples.why: The bare noun 'peruntukan' breaks the parallel with the verb phrases 'menetapkan' and 'memadam'. The verb form 'memperuntukkan' reads naturally.

editor_note: None of the five rewritten entries changes the meaning. Entry 8 keeps the server-side/client-side split and the v0.50.0 caveat intact, and entry 17 keeps its list of options. There are three editor-level slips. "client-side" is "sisi klien" in entry 8 but "bahagian klien" in entries 35 and 36. Entry 38 uses "mitigasi ... ralat" where the rest of the page uses "pengurangan ralat". In entry 17, "number of randomizations" becomes "bilangan rawak", which reads more like "random number(s)" than a count of randomization runs; "bilangan perawakan" would be clearer.

examples.source: with the new client-side Estimator
examples.translation: dengan Estimator bahagian klien yang baharu
examples.suggested: dengan Estimator sisi klien yang baharu
examples.why: Entry 8 renders client-side/server-side as "sisi klien"/"sisi pelayan". Entries 35 and 36 switch to "bahagian klien", so the same concept has two names on one page.

examples.source: Error mitigation and suppression techniques
examples.translation: teknik mitigasi dan penindasan ralat yang tersedia
examples.suggested: teknik pengurangan dan penindasan ralat yang tersedia
examples.why: Entries 6 and 21 render "error mitigation" as "pengurangan ralat". Switching to "mitigasi" here is inconsistent within the file.

examples.source: number of randomizations
examples.translation: bilangan rawak
examples.suggested: bilangan perawakan
examples.why: "bilangan rawak" reads like "random number(s)", not a count of randomizations. The concept is still recognizable, so this is minor, but it is imprecise.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout and nothing here would mislead a learner. The benchmark caveats, the noise degradation at 90–100 qubits and the binary-to-spin mapping example all match the source. The core terms are correct and used consistently: get, litar, Hamiltonan, keadaan asas, ansatz, pasca-pemprosesan. The remaining problems are small. "Shots" is rendered literally as "100,000 tangkapan", which is awkward. The MS violation definition in [26] is a clumsy calque ("sejauh mana penyelesaian daripada memenuhi"). "SWAP-heavy" is calqued as "berat-SWAP", and the greedy-search sentence in [16] is stiff ("mengulangi secara rawak melalui").

examples.source: with the `ibm_boston` device as a backend and 100,000 shots
examples.translation: sebagai backend dan 100,000 tangkapan
examples.suggested: sebagai backend dan 100,000 shot (cubaan pengukuran)
examples.why: 'tangkapan' reads as 'catches/captures'. In this domain 'shots' is usually kept as 'shot' or glossed so the reader recognises it.

examples.source: measures how far the solution is from satisfying all constraints
examples.translation: mengukur sejauh mana penyelesaian daripada memenuhi semua kekangan
examples.suggested: mengukur sejauh mana penyelesaian itu menyimpang daripada memenuhi semua kekangan
examples.why: This follows the English 'how far ... from' word for word and leaves out the verb, so the Malay sentence is incomplete.

examples.source: standard, SWAP-heavy, transpilation methods
examples.translation: kaedah transpilasi standard yang berat-SWAP
examples.suggested: kaedah transpilasi standard yang banyak bergantung pada get SWAP
examples.why: 'berat-SWAP' is a calque of the English compound and does not read naturally in Malay.

examples.source: a local greedy search that iterates randomly through the solution string and flips bit values
examples.translation: carian tamak (greedy) tempatan yang mengulangi secara rawak melalui rentetan penyelesaian
examples.suggested: carian tamak (greedy) tempatan yang melalui rentetan penyelesaian secara rawak dan menterbalikkan nilai bit
examples.why: 'mengulangi ... melalui' is a stiff literal rendering of 'iterates through'. 'menterbalikkan' is also more precise than 'menukar' for flipping a bit.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through, including the caveats in [24] (postselection is not a complete solution, it raises sampling overhead, and relying on it alone is likely insufficient for deeper circuits) and the conservative AND strategy in [20]. A native editor would still fix three things. In [9], 'transpile' becomes the odd coinage 'ditransail' where 'ditranspil' is the usual form. In [20], 'ia lulus oleh kedua-dua strategi' is a passive calque of 'passed by both'. In [24], 'pembatalan ralat kebarangkalian' should use the adjective form, 'pembatalan ralat berkebarangkalian'.

examples.source: to execute and transpile against a backend
examples.translation: untuk dilaksanakan dan ditransail terhadap Backend
examples.suggested: untuk dilaksanakan dan ditranspil terhadap Backend
examples.why: 'ditransail' is a nonstandard coinage. 'transpil/ditranspil' is the recognizable form.

examples.source: retains a shot only if it is passed by both node and edge strategies
examples.translation: mengekalkan tembakan hanya jika ia lulus oleh kedua-dua strategi nod dan tepi
examples.suggested: mengekalkan tembakan hanya jika tembakan itu diterima oleh kedua-dua strategi nod dan tepi
examples.why: 'lulus oleh' is a calque of the English passive and reads stiffly.

examples.source: probabilistic error cancellation
examples.translation: pembatalan ralat kebarangkalian
examples.suggested: pembatalan ralat berkebarangkalian
examples.why: 'kebarangkalian' is the noun 'probability'. The adjectival form fits the name of the technique (PEC).

editor_note: Nothing here would mislead a learner, but "deploy" is translated three different ways and one of them is wrong. In [3] and [18] it becomes "digunakan"/"menggunakan", which means "used", so the sentence in [18] now points to a guide on *using* the template instead of *deploying* it. In [19] it becomes "Sebarkan". In [8], "dianjurkan" is the wrong word for "organized" ("disusun" is right), and "Kini termasuk dalam koleksi ialah" copies the English word order. The title in [1] also drops "Pengenalan kepada", even though the heading in [2] keeps it.

examples.source: Read through the guide on deploying the function template for a chemistry workflow
examples.translation: Baca panduan tentang menggunakan templat fungsi untuk aliran kerja kimia
examples.suggested: Baca panduan tentang mengerahkan (deploy) templat fungsi untuk aliran kerja kimia
examples.why: 'menggunakan' means 'using', not 'deploying'. The guide is about deploying to Qiskit Serverless, and 'using' hides that. It also doesn't match 'Sebarkan' in [19].

examples.source: All templates are readily deployable to Qiskit Serverless
examples.translation: Semua templat boleh digunakan secara terus ke Qiskit Serverless
examples.suggested: Semua templat sedia untuk dikerahkan ke Qiskit Serverless
examples.why: 'digunakan ... ke' ('used ... to') is ungrammatical and loses the meaning of deployment.

examples.source: Qiskit Function template implementations are organized by application area. Currently included in the collection are two physics templates
examples.translation: Implementasi templat Fungsi Qiskit dianjurkan mengikut bidang aplikasi. Kini termasuk dalam koleksi ialah dua templat fizik
examples.suggested: Implementasi templat Fungsi Qiskit disusun mengikut bidang aplikasi. Koleksi ini kini merangkumi dua templat fizik
examples.why: 'dianjurkan' means 'organized' as in hosting an event, or 'recommended', so it is the wrong word for 'arranged'. The second clause copies the English inverted word order.

examples.source: Introduction to Qiskit Function templates
examples.translation: Templat Fungsi Qiskit
examples.suggested: Pengenalan kepada templat Fungsi Qiskit
examples.why: The title drops 'Introduction to', so it no longer matches the heading in [2].

editor_note: Entry 8 renders "dynamical decoupling" as "penyahgandingan dinamik", which is a faithful, standard DBP-style Malay term, and it keeps the link target and the list-item lowercase unchanged.

All nine rewritten entries match the English and read naturally: entry 21 keeps the twirling shot-count rule ("hasil darab `num_randomizations` dan `shots_per_randomization` ... digunakan"), entry 58 renders "ground state" as "keadaan asas", and the API-link labels consistently use "Dokumentasi API `...`".

Entry 23 is accurate: "Penyahgandingan dinamik" is a correct, well-formed Malay rendering of "dynamical decoupling" (penyahgandingan = de-coupling), and it does not mislead. The only problem is consistency. The sentence just before it (entry 22) keeps the technique in English ("pilihan lalai untuk dynamical decoupling dan twirling"), and the sibling heading in entry 24 stays "Twirling". A reader who meets the English term in the prose then gets a Malay-only heading. The fix is either to add the English gloss to the heading, or to use the Malay term in entry 22 as well.

examples.source: Dynamical decoupling {#dynamical-decoupling}
examples.translation: Penyahgandingan dinamik {#dynamical-decoupling}
examples.suggested: Penyahgandingan dinamik (dynamical decoupling) {#dynamical-decoupling}
examples.why: The rendering is correct, but entry 22 names the same technique in English as 'dynamical decoupling' and the parallel heading 'Twirling' stays in English. The term is used inconsistently within the file. Adding the English gloss connects the heading to the prose.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through, including both key constraints: Estimator circuits "tidak boleh" contain measurements and Sampler circuits "mesti" contain them. "precision"/"shots" as sampling overhead also comes through. A native editor would still fix some small slips. "instance" is rendered as "contoh" ("Cipta contoh", "contoh objek"), which reads as "example". "Initialize" is rendered as "Mulakan" (start) instead of "Awalkan". Noise is "hingar" in [6] but "berbising" in [47]. Some calques remain: "mereka" is used as a pronoun for the primitives, and "di mana" is used as a relative clause in [40].

examples.source: Instantiate a qiskit.primitives.StatevectorEstimator.
examples.translation: Cipta contoh qiskit.primitives.StatevectorEstimator.
examples.suggested: Cipta tika (instance) qiskit.primitives.StatevectorEstimator.
examples.why: 'contoh' normally means 'example'. A learner could read this as 'create an example' instead of 'create an instance'. The same issue appears in [21] and [36].

examples.source: Initialize Estimator
examples.translation: Mulakan Estimator
examples.suggested: Awalkan Estimator
examples.why: 'Mulakan' means start/begin, not initialize. The same issue appears in [35].

examples.source: Exact and noisy simulation with Qiskit Aer primitives
examples.translation: Simulasi tepat dan berbising dengan primitif Qiskit Aer
examples.suggested: Simulasi tepat dan berhingar dengan primitif Qiskit Aer
examples.why: This file uses 'hingar' for noise elsewhere ([6], [47] 'model hingar'). 'berbising' is inconsistent with that and sounds colloquial.

examples.source: preserving the shot order in which they were measured
examples.translation: mengekalkan susunan shot di mana ia diukur
examples.suggested: mengekalkan susunan shot semasa ia diukur
examples.why: 'di mana' used as a relative pronoun is a calque of English 'in which'.

examples.source: as they rely on local statevector simulations
examples.translation: kerana mereka bergantung pada simulasi statevector tempatan
examples.suggested: kerana ia bergantung pada simulasi statevector tempatan
examples.why: 'mereka' is for people. For non-human referents, standard Malay uses 'ia'. The same issue appears in [34].

editor_note: Entry 23 matches the English, including the 30-day window, the billing-information requirement and the emphasised "*tidak akan dicaj*" caveat, and it keeps "percubaan" for trial and "pengebilan" for billing, the same as entries 19 and 21-22.

The Malay is faithful and reads naturally in the "anda" register, and the key facts are kept exactly: pass mark 16 of 20 ("sekurang-kurangnya 16 dengan betul"), the lock after two failed attempts ("dikunci buat sementara waktu"), and "menduduki peperiksaan lencana" for the badging exam.

The meaning is faithful throughout: the partial-measurement example and the point about entanglement (belitan) are both intact, and nothing would mislead a learner. A few phrases in [5] and [6] are English calques that a native editor would rewrite. In [5], 'dalam memasuki pelajaran ini' and the relative clause 'yang mana perbincangan ... boleh digunakan' follow the English syntax. In [6], 'terdapat lebih banyak perkara untuk memahami ... daripada sekadar mengiktiraf' is stiff, and 'mengiktiraf' means formal acknowledgement, not 'recognizing/realizing' (menyedari).

examples.source: There is, however, more to understanding multiple quantum systems than simply recognizing that they may be viewed collectively as single systems.
examples.translation: Walau bagaimanapun, terdapat lebih banyak perkara untuk memahami sistem kuantum berbilang daripada sekadar mengiktiraf bahawa ia boleh dilihat secara kolektif sebagai sistem tunggal.
examples.suggested: Walau bagaimanapun, memahami sistem kuantum berbilang memerlukan lebih daripada sekadar menyedari bahawa ia boleh dilihat secara kolektif sebagai satu sistem tunggal.
examples.why: This copies the English 'there is more to X than Y' structure word for word. Also, 'mengiktiraf' means official recognition or acknowledgement, not realizing something.

examples.source: ...as if they form a single, compound system — to which the discussion in the previous lesson applies.
examples.translation: ...seolah-olah ia membentuk satu sistem tunggal yang digabungkan — yang mana perbincangan dalam pelajaran sebelumnya boleh digunakan.
examples.suggested: ...seolah-olah ia membentuk satu sistem majmuk tunggal — dan perbincangan dalam pelajaran sebelumnya terpakai kepadanya.
examples.why: Using 'yang mana' as a relative pronoun is a well-known calque of English 'to which'. 'Terpakai kepadanya' is the idiomatic way to say 'applies to'.

examples.source: it is important to understand exactly how when analyzing quantum algorithms and protocols.
examples.translation: penting untuk memahami dengan tepat bagaimana apabila menganalisis algoritma dan protokol kuantum.
examples.suggested: penting untuk memahami dengan tepat bagaimana hal ini berlaku apabila menganalisis algoritma dan protokol kuantum.
examples.why: The bare 'bagaimana' without a verb copies the English ellipsis and reads as incomplete in Malay.

editor_note: The translation is faithful and reads naturally, with defensible term choices such as litar kuantum, pengukuran projektif, teorem tiada-pengklonan and "membezakan keadaan kuantum bukan-ortogon dengan sempurna", and none of them changes the meaning of the source.

The meaning is faithful throughout this short overview and nothing would mislead a learner. There are two small editorial slips. The heading "Sasaran audiens" [7] follows English word order: Malay puts the head noun first, so it should read "Audiens sasaran" (or "Sasaran pembaca/peserta"). Entry [5] also leaves out "effectively" from "effectively build the necessary capabilities", which slightly weakens the course's stated aim.

examples.source: Intended audience
examples.translation: Sasaran audiens
examples.suggested: Audiens sasaran
examples.why: This follows English modifier-first order. Malay puts the head noun first, and as written it reads more like 'the audience's target'.

examples.source: to effectively build the necessary capabilities to successfully kick-start quantum initiatives
examples.translation: membina keupayaan yang diperlukan bagi memulakan inisiatif kuantum dengan jayanya
examples.suggested: membina keupayaan yang diperlukan secara berkesan bagi memulakan inisiatif kuantum dengan jayanya
examples.why: The translation drops the qualifier 'effectively'. This is a minor loss of emphasis and does not mislead.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful overall. The core argument comes through intact: syndrome measurement projects the error onto a Pauli error, and the entropy moves into the syndrome qubits, rendered as "memproyeksikan", "kerawakan — atau entropi". In [9], "we tensor the unitary matrix with the identity matrix" becomes the vague "mengoperasikan matriks unitari dengan matriks identiti", which drops the tensor-product operation. The formula beside it keeps this from misleading a learner. Smaller slips: [8] renders "the numbers α, β…" as "bilangan" (a count) where "nombor" is needed, and "generalization" appears as both "Pengitlakan" (heading [41]) and "digeneralisasikan" ([42]).

examples.source: where in each case we tensor the unitary matrix with the identity matrix on every other qubit
examples.translation: di mana dalam setiap kes kita mengoperasikan matriks unitari dengan matriks identiti pada setiap qubit lain
examples.suggested: di mana dalam setiap kes kita mengambil hasil darab tensor matriks unitari dengan matriks identiti pada setiap qubit lain
examples.why: 'mengoperasikan ... dengan' does not name the tensor product, which is the specific construction being described. It is vague but not false, and the formula alongside shows it.

examples.source: the numbers $\alpha$, $\beta$, $\gamma$, and $\delta$ must satisfy
examples.translation: bilangan $\alpha,$ $\beta,$ $\gamma,$ dan $\delta$ mesti memenuhi
examples.suggested: nombor-nombor $\alpha,$ $\beta,$ $\gamma,$ dan $\delta$ mesti memenuhi
examples.why: 'bilangan' means a count or quantity. The complex coefficients are 'nombor'.

examples.source: The discretization of errors generalizes to other quantum error-correcting codes
examples.translation: Pendiskretan ralat digeneralisasikan kepada kod pembetulan ralat kuantum yang lain
examples.suggested: Pendiskretan ralat dapat diitlakkan kepada kod pembetulan ralat kuantum yang lain
examples.why: The heading [41] uses 'Pengitlakan' but the body switches to 'digeneralisasikan'. The term should be consistent, and the passive form also reads stiffly.

examples.source: the system on the right, which is the one we care about
examples.translation: sistem di sebelah kanan, iaitu yang kita pedulikan
examples.suggested: sistem di sebelah kanan, iaitu sistem yang penting bagi kita
examples.why: 'yang kita pedulikan' is a calque that sounds colloquial and awkward in technical prose.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout: the quadratic and square-root claims in [3], the caveat about practical advantage in [5] and the FFT/quicksort comparison in [6] all survive, and nothing would mislead a learner. A few phrases are stiff or calqued. "boleh membolehkan" is redundant, "pasti akan hilang oleh kelajuan jam" is an awkward passive, "Memang" is a weak rendering of "Indeed", and "masih sangat awal" is missing a noun like "peringkat". Also, "we should not be so quick to underestimate" became "tidak seharusnya terlalu meremehkan", which loses the idea of being too quick, and "ulasan semula" is an odd word for "refresher".

examples.source: we should not be so quick to underestimate the potential of technological advances that could allow
examples.translation: kita tidak seharusnya terlalu meremehkan potensi kemajuan teknologi yang boleh membolehkan
examples.suggested: kita tidak seharusnya terlalu cepat memandang rendah potensi kemajuan teknologi yang mungkin membolehkan
examples.why: It drops the sense of being too hasty ('so quick'), and 'boleh membolehkan' is a redundant calque.

examples.source: is sure to be washed away by the staggering clock speeds
examples.translation: pasti akan hilang oleh kelajuan jam komputer klasik moden yang luar biasa
examples.suggested: pasti akan ditenggelami oleh kelajuan jam komputer klasik moden yang luar biasa
examples.why: 'hilang oleh' is an ungrammatical passive calque. 'ditenggelami oleh' or 'terhapus oleh' reads naturally.

examples.source: Indeed, ... still very much in its infancy
examples.translation: Memang, ... masih sangat awal berbanding pengiraan klasik
examples.suggested: Malah, ... masih di peringkat awal berbanding pengiraan klasik
examples.why: 'Memang,' at the start of the sentence is conversational, and 'masih sangat awal' needs a noun such as 'peringkat'.

examples.source: begins with a refresher of the unstructured search problem
examples.translation: memulakan dengan ulasan semula masalah pencarian tanpa struktur
examples.suggested: memulakan dengan imbasan semula masalah pencarian tanpa struktur
examples.why: 'ulasan semula' suggests a re-review or critique, while 'imbasan semula' is the natural word for a refresher.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful and nothing here would mislead a learner. The core terms are correct: phase estimation→anggaran fasa, quantum Fourier transform→jelmaan Fourier kuantum, integer factorization→pemfaktoran integer, discrete logarithm→logaritma diskret. Two idioms are copied too literally from English. In the video title [6], "Dengan ini di tangan" is a word-for-word calque of "With this in hand", and "membimbing melalui prosedur" has no object. In [3], "Dalam perjalanan itu" translates "Along the way" literally and would read better as "Sepanjang pelajaran ini".

examples.source: With this in hand, John moves on to Shor's algorithm.
examples.translation: Dengan ini di tangan, John beralih kepada algoritma Shor.
examples.suggested: Berbekalkan hasil ini, John beralih kepada algoritma Shor.
examples.why: This copies the English idiom word for word. A Malay technical writer would write 'Berbekalkan' or 'Setelah itu'.

examples.source: Along the way, we'll encounter the quantum Fourier transform
examples.translation: Dalam perjalanan itu, kita akan menemui jelmaan Fourier kuantum
examples.suggested: Sepanjang pelajaran ini, kita akan menemui jelmaan Fourier kuantum
examples.why: 'Dalam perjalanan itu' is a literal copy of 'along the way' and sounds stiff in teaching prose.

editor_note: Entry [44] turns the probabilistic claim "it's unlikely that we'll get the same function value" into "tidak mungkin kita mendapat", which means "it is impossible". That contradicts the next paragraph ([45]), which says the error probability is 2^{-k+1}, so a learner could come away thinking random sampling never fails. [42] also weakens "exponentially many queries" to "pertanyaan yang amat banyak" ("very many queries"), and [105] renders "highly contrived" as "sangat direka-bentuk" ("very designed"). Smaller problems: "query" switches from "pertanyaan" to "kueri" halfway through the file, [36] leaves "constant"/"balanced" in English where the rest of the file uses malar/seimbang, and there are calques such as "tangkapan" for "catch" and "dirawat" for "treated".

examples.source: it's unlikely that we'll get the same function value for all of them when $f$ is balanced
examples.translation: tidak mungkin kita mendapat nilai fungsi yang sama untuk semua daripadanya apabila $f$ adalah seimbang
examples.suggested: kecil kemungkinan kita mendapat nilai fungsi yang sama untuk semuanya apabila $f$ seimbang
examples.why: 'tidak mungkin' means impossible. This overstates the claim and contradicts the nonzero error probability 2^{-k+1} given in [45].

examples.source: must make exponentially many queries
examples.translation: mesti membuat pertanyaan yang amat banyak
examples.suggested: mesti membuat bilangan pertanyaan yang eksponen (secara eksponen banyak)
examples.why: The rendering drops 'exponentially', the key complexity claim the section is built on.

examples.source: This is a highly contrived problem
examples.translation: Ini adalah masalah yang sangat direka-bentuk
examples.suggested: Ini ialah masalah yang sangat dibuat-buat
examples.why: 'direka-bentuk' means 'designed'. It loses the point that the problem is artificial.

examples.source: The query gate is then performed
examples.translation: Gate kueri kemudian dilakukan
examples.suggested: Use one term for 'query' throughout (pertanyaan or kueri)
examples.why: Entries [3]-[48] use 'pertanyaan' and entries [71]-[106] use 'kueri' for the same concept.

examples.source: There is a catch, however
examples.translation: Walau bagaimanapun, terdapat satu tangkapan
examples.suggested: Walau bagaimanapun, ada kelemahannya
examples.why: 'tangkapan' is a literal calque of 'catch' (as in a physical catch) and reads oddly here.

editor_note: Nothing here would mislead a learner. The meaning is faithful throughout: 20 questions, a pass mark of 16, the lock after two failed attempts, and the Credly data-sharing notice all match the English. There are two small wording issues. In [12], "menerbitkan lencana" (to issue a badge) uses the verb for publishing a book, and a native editor would write "mengeluarkan lencana". The course title is left in English in [5] ("General formulation of quantum information") but translated in [7] ("Formulasi umum maklumat kuantum"), so the page is inconsistent.

examples.source: In order to issue you an IBM Digital Badge ... used to issue your badge
examples.translation: Untuk menerbitkan IBM Digital Badge kepada anda ... digunakan untuk menerbitkan lencana anda
examples.suggested: Untuk mengeluarkan IBM Digital Badge kepada anda ... digunakan untuk mengeluarkan lencana anda
examples.why: 'Menerbitkan' means to publish a book or document. For certificates and badges, 'mengeluarkan' is the usual Malay verb.

examples.source: Congratulations on completing the "General formulation of quantum information" course
examples.translation: Tahniah kerana melengkapkan kursus "General formulation of quantum information"
examples.suggested: Tahniah kerana melengkapkan kursus "Formulasi umum maklumat kuantum"

editor_note: The meaning is faithful everywhere. The pass mark (16 of 20), the temporary lock after two failed attempts and the Credly privacy caveats all carry over accurately. The one defect is a register slip in the privacy notice [11]: it switches to casual "Kamu akan menerima pemberitahuan e-mel" when the rest of the page, including the same paragraph, uses the standard "anda". Keeping the course title in English ("Integrating quantum and high-performance computing") is a defensible choice.

examples.source: You will receive an email notification from Credly with instructions for claiming the badge.
examples.translation: Kamu akan menerima pemberitahuan e-mel daripada Credly dengan arahan untuk menuntut lencana tersebut.
examples.suggested: Anda akan menerima pemberitahuan e-mel daripada Credly dengan arahan untuk menuntut lencana tersebut.
examples.why: The casual 'kamu' breaks the standard 'anda' register used everywhere else on the page, including in the surrounding sentences of this same formal privacy notice.

editor_note: The meaning matches the English throughout and nothing would mislead a learner. The course description, the two audience groups (quantum without HPC, and HPC without quantum), the exam and badge flow, and the Credly privacy notice all keep their content, including "IBM mungkin berkongsi". The one slip is in entry [0]: "satu aliran kerja tunggal" says "single" twice, so "dalam satu aliran kerja" or "dalam aliran kerja tunggal" alone would read naturally. The register uses "anda" consistently.

examples.source: can be combined in a single workflow.
examples.translation: boleh digabungkan dalam satu aliran kerja tunggal.
examples.suggested: boleh digabungkan dalam satu aliran kerja.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. The pass mark ("sekurang-kurangnya 16" of 20), the two-attempt lockout ("dikunci sementara") and the Credly privacy notice all match the English. The second-person pronoun is capitalised inconsistently: entries [0], [6], [7], [8], [9] and [12] use "Anda", but [5] uses lowercase "anda" ("Maklum balas anda"). Separately, "untuk menavigasi ke IBM Training" in [7] is a slightly stiff calque of "navigate to". A native editor would write "untuk ke laman IBM Training" or "untuk pergi ke IBM Training".

examples.source: Your feedback will be used to enhance our content offering
examples.translation: Maklum balas anda akan digunakan untuk menambah baik tawaran kandungan
examples.suggested: Maklum balas Anda akan digunakan untuk menambah baik tawaran kandungan

examples.source: click the button below to navigate to IBM® Training
examples.translation: klik butang di bawah untuk menavigasi ke IBM® Training
examples.suggested: klik butang di bawah untuk pergi ke IBM® Training
examples.why: 'menavigasi ke' is a literal calque of 'navigate to'. Natural Malay UI prose would say 'pergi ke' or 'ke laman'.

editor_note: Entry 4 is faithful and reads naturally. "intended audience" becomes "khalayak sasaran" and "utility era" becomes "era utiliti", and "hukum Moore" matches the section heading in [38].

Entry 64 is faithful and natural. It says "primitif EstimatorV2 dengan backend palsu", "litar Trotter garis dasar" and "boleh cerap ZZ bagi setiap litar", matching the terms used in entries 41, 42 and 62. Outside this delta, entry 37 ("The Hamiltonian is as follows:") has a Malay string that repeats entry 36's paragraph instead of translating it. That entry needs a separate fix.

Nothing here would mislead a learner. The meaning is faithful, including the two-plus-two swaps, the depth reduced by more than half, and the 9^3 sampling overhead. The same quasi-probability term appears two ways: "taburan quasikemungkinan" in [23] and "taburan kuasi-kebarangkalian" in [30] and [33]. In [24], "arbitrarily chosen" became "dipilih secara rawak" (randomly chosen), which is a small change of nuance. In [17], "pass manager" became "pengurus laluan preset", a literal reading of "pass" as route or path that is recognizable but stiff.

examples.source: the decomposed gates' joint quasiprobability distribution
examples.translation: taburan quasikemungkinan bersama gate yang diuraikan
examples.suggested: taburan kuasi-kebarangkalian bersama bagi gate yang diuraikan
examples.why: Entries [30] and [33] use 'kuasi-kebarangkalian'. This one mixes the English spelling 'quasi' with 'kemungkinan' instead of 'kebarangkalian'.

examples.source: an example of an arbitrarily chosen subexperiment
examples.translation: contoh subeksperimen yang dipilih secara rawak
examples.suggested: contoh subeksperimen yang dipilih secara sembarangan
examples.why: 'Arbitrarily' means any one picked for illustration, not picked at random. The difference is minor, but in a page about probabilistic sampling it could suggest a random draw.

examples.source: available with a preset pass manager
examples.translation: yang tersedia dengan pengurus laluan preset
examples.suggested: yang tersedia dengan pass manager pratetap
examples.why: 'Laluan' means route or path, which does not match the compiler-pass sense. Qiskit usually keeps 'pass manager' in English.

editor_note: The translation is faithful overall. The MIS formulation, the clique-to-one-hot XY-mixer explanation, pendant nodes and the fixed-angle warm-starting passage all keep their meaning, and core terms (litar, kekangan, pemboleh ubah kendur, bucu/tepi) are consistent. The minor issues are these. "Problem instance" is rendered three ways: "contoh" in [15], [36] and [39], and the English "instance" in [42]; "contoh" also reads as "example". Entry [15] drops "even" ("even for graphs with a few hundred nodes"), which weakens the point about how hard the problem is. There are also a few stiff phrasings: "import ia" in [83] and "telah dilaksanakan lebih awal" for "pre-implemented" in [47].

examples.source: This example uses the `es60fst02` instance from QOBLIB
examples.translation: Contoh ini menggunakan instance `es60fst02` daripada QOBLIB
examples.suggested: Contoh ini menggunakan tika `es60fst02` daripada QOBLIB (or use one rendering consistently with [15]/[36]/[39])
examples.why: "Instance" is left in English here but rendered as "contoh" in [15], [36] and [39]. That is inconsistent, and "contoh" collides with "Contoh ini" (this example) in the same sentence.

examples.source: and even for graphs with a few hundred nodes specific instances become difficult to solve
examples.translation: dan bagi graf dengan beberapa ratus nod, contoh tertentu menjadi sukar untuk diselesaikan
examples.suggested: dan bahkan bagi graf dengan hanya beberapa ratus nod, sesetengah contoh menjadi sukar untuk diselesaikan

examples.source: After installation of the `luna-model` PyPI package, import it as follows:
examples.translation: Selepas pemasangan pakej PyPI `luna-model`, import ia seperti berikut:
examples.suggested: Selepas memasang pakej PyPI `luna-model`, import pakej tersebut seperti berikut:

examples.suggested: menyediakan kelas aplikasi sedia ada

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through, including the fault-tolerance and exponential-depth claims in [44], [47] and [50], so nothing here would mislead a learner. There are a few wording slips a native editor would fix. The heading "Proses selepas" in [40] is a calque of "post-process"; "Pascaproses" is the standard word. [26] slips into colloquial "dah". Runtime appears as "masa larian" in [4] but "masa jalan" in [15]. "Near-term" is rendered "jangka pendek" in [52], which reads as "short-term" rather than "near-term".

examples.source: Step 4: Post-process and return result in desired classical format
examples.translation: Langkah 4: Proses selepas dan kembalikan keputusan dalam format klasik yang dikehendaki
examples.suggested: Langkah 4: Pascaproses dan kembalikan keputusan dalam format klasik yang dikehendaki
examples.why: "Proses selepas" is a word-for-word calque. "Pascaproses" is the conventional Malay technical term.

examples.source: Now that we have the oracle function, we can define a specific instance of Grover search.
examples.translation: Sekarang kita dah ada fungsi oracle, kita boleh takrifkan instans carian Grover yang tertentu.
examples.suggested: Setelah kita mempunyai fungsi oracle, kita boleh mentakrifkan instans carian Grover yang tertentu.
examples.why: "dah" is colloquial spoken Malay and breaks the standard written register used everywhere else in the file.

examples.source: The runtime `Sampler` primitive allows seamless execution of Grover circuits.
examples.translation: Primitif `Sampler` masa jalan membolehkan pelaksanaan Circuit Grover dengan lancar.
examples.suggested: Primitif `Sampler` Qiskit Runtime membolehkan Circuit Grover dilaksanakan dengan lancar.
examples.why: Here "runtime" is the product name, and it becomes "masa jalan", while [4] uses "masa larian" for runtime. The rendering is inconsistent and blurs the product name.

examples.source: give near-term examples of optimization with quantum computers
examples.translation: memberikan contoh jangka pendek pengoptimuman dengan komputer kuantum
examples.suggested: memberikan contoh pengoptimuman dengan komputer kuantum jangka terdekat
examples.why: "jangka pendek" means short-term, but "near-term" here means the current and upcoming generation of hardware. "jangka terdekat" is the closer rendering.

editor_note: One sentence is misleading. In [11], the caveat that implicit-solvent results are "more approximate" (less accurate) than explicit-solvent models is rendered "akan lebih menghampiri berbanding rakan sepadannya". In Malay that most naturally reads as "will come closer than its counterpart", which suggests the cheap model is more accurate and reverses the trade-off. Besides that, the file is inconsistent: quantum/kuantum, tersirat/implisit ([13]), methylamine/metilamina, and kita/kami ([43]). There are also calques: "yang itu sendiri", "katakan", "adalah membantu", "rakan sepadannya", and "penutupan peranti pertengahan-pelaksanaan".

examples.source: although the end result will generally be more approximate than the counterpart: more computationally costly explicit solvent models
examples.translation: walaupun hasil akhir secara amnya akan lebih menghampiri berbanding rakan sepadannya: model pelarut jelas yang lebih mahal
examples.suggested: walaupun hasil akhirnya secara amnya kurang tepat (lebih bersifat anggaran) berbanding alternatifnya, iaitu model pelarut eksplisit yang lebih mahal secara pengiraan
examples.why: 'lebih menghampiri' reads as 'closer (to the true value)'. That turns the accuracy caveat around, so the cheap implicit model sounds more accurate than the explicit one.

examples.source: combining quantum electronic-structure calculations with an implicit solvent model ... methylamine-in-water
examples.translation: pengiraan struktur elektronik kuantum dengan model pelarut implisit ... metilamina-dalam-air
examples.suggested: Pick one form of each term and use it throughout the file: kuantum, tersirat (or implisit), metilamina.
examples.why: Elsewhere the file uses 'quantum' ([0],[7],[12]), 'tersirat' and 'methylamine' ([12]), so each term appears in two forms.

examples.source: This is important to biophysical models used, say, in drug discovery ... it is helpful to model
examples.translation: Ini penting kepada model biofizik yang digunakan, katakan, dalam penemuan ubat ... adalah membantu untuk memodelkan
examples.suggested: Ini penting bagi model biofizik yang digunakan, misalnya, dalam penemuan ubat ... lebih baik memodelkan
examples.why: 'katakan' and 'adalah membantu' are word-for-word English calques. So is 'yang itu sendiri' earlier in the same paragraph.

examples.source: Here, we combine Step 3 (Execute) and Step 4
examples.translation: Di sini, kami menggabungkan Langkah 3
examples.suggested: Di sini, kita menggabungkan Langkah 3
examples.why: The rest of the page uses the inclusive 'kita'. This entry switches to 'kami'.

editor_note: Entry 60 is faithful and natural. It renders the survey note as "Kaji selidik ini oleh IBM Quantum ... kandungan tutorial (ditulis oleh IBM)", uses "pelaksanaan kod" for code execution and "maklum balas mengenainya" for feedback on those, and keeps the GitHub-issue link intact.

The main problem is "entangling layer(s)", which is rendered as "lapisan penyepaduan" in [48], [62] and [70]. "Penyepaduan" means integration or unification, not entanglement ("keterjeratan"), so a learner cannot tell these are the two-qubit entangling layers whose noise PEA learns. That is a concept-level mistranslation, like the rubric's "variational" to "permutational" example. Smaller issues: "fidelity" becomes "ketepatan" (accuracy) in [33]. "Extrapolation" is spelled both "ekstrapolasi" and "extrapolasi" ([82]-[99]), with a stray English "(extrapolated)" left in [78]. "Mitigated" switches between "dikurangkan ralatnya" and "dimitigasi", and "noisy" appears as "berderau" next to "hingar". In [97], "demonstrating the utility" is strengthened to "membuktikan keberkesanan" ("proves the effectiveness").

examples.source: Define entangling layer couplings
examples.translation: Tentukan gandingan lapisan penyepaduan
examples.suggested: Tentukan gandingan lapisan pengjeratan (lapisan yang menjeratkan qubit)
examples.why: 'Penyepaduan' means integration/unification, not entanglement ('keterjeratan'). This error repeats in [62] and [70], so the learner never sees that these are entangling two-qubit layers.

examples.source: Derive a fidelity (error for each noise channel)
examples.translation: Terbitkan ketepatan (ralat bagi setiap saluran hingar)
examples.suggested: Terbitkan fideliti (ralat bagi setiap saluran hingar)
examples.why: Fidelity is a specific quantum quantity. 'Ketepatan' means accuracy/precision.

examples.source: both mitigated (extrapolated) and raw
examples.translation: sama ada yang dimitigasi (extrapolated) mahupun yang mentah
examples.suggested: sama ada yang telah dikurangkan ralatnya (diekstrapolasi) mahupun yang mentah
examples.why: English is left inside the brackets. 'Mitigated' switches between 'dikurangkan ralatnya' and 'dimitigasi' within the same paragraph, and later entries use the misspelling 'extrapolasi' instead of 'ekstrapolasi'.

examples.source: demonstrating the utility of the PEA-based mitigation technique
examples.translation: membuktikan keberkesanan teknik mitigasi berasaskan PEA ini
examples.suggested: menunjukkan kegunaan teknik mitigasi berasaskan PEA ini
examples.why: 'Demonstrating' is strengthened to 'proves'. 'Nilai berderau' in the same sentence also clashes with 'hingar', which the rest of the file uses for 'noise'.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. The key facts carry over correctly: the O(N^2) and N(N+1)/2 entry counts, row 15/column 20, and "darker red indicates fidelities closer to 1.0". A few renderings still need an editor. In [24], "exact (up to shot noise)" becomes "tepat (sehingga bunyi tembakan)", which calques "shot noise" as the sound of gunfire and turns "up to" into "until". In [28], "special unitary group" becomes "kumpulan unit istimewa" rather than the conventional "kumpulan unitari khas"; "unit" also points to a different algebraic idea, the group of units. "circuit" is split between "litar" ([8], [18], [30]) and a kept "circuit" ([36], [45]), and [15] opens with the calque "Adalah juga berguna".

examples.source: A statevector simulator is exact (up to shot noise)
examples.translation: Simulator statevector adalah tepat (sehingga bunyi tembakan)
examples.suggested: Simulator statevector adalah tepat (kecuali hingar tembakan / shot noise)
examples.why: 'bunyi tembakan' literally means the sound of gunshots, and 'sehingga' reads as 'until'. The caveat that the result is exact apart from sampling noise is blurred.

examples.source: which is the special unitary group of 2 × 2 matrices
examples.translation: iaitu kumpulan unit istimewa daripada matriks 2 × 2
examples.suggested: iaitu kumpulan unitari khas bagi matriks 2 × 2
examples.why: 'unit' is not 'unitari'. In algebra, 'kumpulan unit' suggests the group of units, and the conventional rendering of SU(n) is 'kumpulan unitari khas'.

examples.source: on the overlap circuit
examples.translation: pada circuit tindihan
examples.suggested: pada litar tindihan
examples.why: 'circuit' is rendered as 'litar' elsewhere in the file ([8], [18], [30]), so this is an inconsistency within the file.

examples.source: It is also useful to have a basic understanding of group theory.
examples.translation: Adalah juga berguna untuk mempunyai pemahaman asas tentang teori kumpulan.
examples.suggested: Pemahaman asas tentang teori kumpulan juga berguna.
examples.why: 'Adalah ... untuk mempunyai' is a calque of the English 'It is ... to have' construction and reads stiffly.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout, including the right/left-half Hamming-weight condition in [57] and the initial_occupancies caveat in [60], but the key terms are inconsistent. "Diagonalization" appears as both "pepenjuruan" ([0], [12], [14]) and the non-standard "penyepelasan/menyepelasi" ([1] page title, [15], [71]). "Noisy/noise" has three renderings: "bermasalah" ("problematic") in [0], [12], [30], [58], [60] and [62], the literal "bunyi" ("sound") in [30], [51] and [58], and the correct "hingar" in [66]. "Ground state" is mostly "keadaan dasar" but becomes "keadaan asas" in [13], which clashes with "keadaan asas" meaning "basis states" in [19]. "Basis set" is both "set asas" ([46]) and "set basis" ([66]).

examples.source: Sample-based quantum diagonalization of a chemistry Hamiltonian
examples.translation: Penyepelasan kuantum berasaskan sampel bagi Hamiltonian kimia
examples.suggested: Pepenjuruan kuantum berasaskan sampel bagi Hamiltonian kimia
examples.why: 'Penyepelasan' is not a standard Malay term. The page's own description [0] and body [12] use the standard 'pepenjuruan', so the title and body disagree.

examples.source: ...using noisy quantum hardware.
examples.translation: ...menggunakan perkakasan kuantum yang bermasalah.
examples.suggested: ...menggunakan perkakasan kuantum yang berhingar.
examples.why: 'Bermasalah' means faulty or problematic, which loses the idea of quantum noise. Elsewhere noise is 'bunyi' (acoustic sound) or 'hingar'. Use 'hingar' consistently.

examples.source: ...fixed particle number and spin Z in the noiseless setting.
examples.translation: ...yang tetap dalam tetapan tanpa bunyi.
examples.suggested: ...yang tetap dalam keadaan tanpa hingar.
examples.why: 'Bunyi' is a literal calque meaning audible sound. The technical term is 'hingar', which the file itself uses in [66].

examples.source: Calculating the ground state of an isolated nitrogen molecule...
examples.translation: Mengira keadaan asas bagi molekul nitrogen terasing...
examples.suggested: Mengira keadaan dasar bagi molekul nitrogen terasing...
examples.why: The rest of the file uses 'keadaan dasar' for ground state, and 'keadaan asas' is used in [19] for basis states, so this mixes two different concepts.

examples.source: a gate set that the LUCJ ansatz naturally decomposes to
examples.translation: set gate yang secara semula jadi terurai oleh ansatz LUCJ
examples.suggested: set gate yang menjadi hasil penguraian semula jadi ansatz LUCJ
examples.why: The passive 'terurai oleh ansatz' reads as if the gate set is decomposed by the ansatz. The direction is reversed and the phrasing is awkward.

editor_note: The page's central concept, the multiplicative "order" of a modulo N, is rendered as "perintah" in entries [14]–[29]. "Perintah" means a command or instruction, so "masalah pencarian perintah" reads as "command-finding problem". From [56] onward the same concept switches to "peringkat", which is the correct mathematical term, with nothing linking the two words. A learner cannot tell that "perintah r" and "peringkat r" are the same quantity. Smaller errors: "coprime" is the non-word "koprosa" in [25] but "koprim" in [59]; "periodicity" is "kekala" (which means permanence) in [22]; the noun "runs" is the verb "jalankan" in [60] and [67]; and "entanglement" is the truncated "keterjalin" in [72].

examples.source: utilizes an intermediary problem known as the *order finding* problem
examples.translation: masalah pertengahan yang dikenali sebagai masalah *pencarian perintah*
examples.suggested: masalah *pencarian peringkat* (order finding), used throughout the file
examples.why: 'Perintah' means command/instruction, not the group-theoretic order of an element. It teaches a false concept, and it conflicts with 'peringkat', which is used for the same r from entry [56] onward.

examples.source: attempt to find $k$ and the order $r$
examples.translation: untuk cuba mencari $k$ dan peringkat $r$
examples.suggested: Use one term ('peringkat') for 'order' everywhere, including entries [14]–[29] and the heading in [24].
examples.why: The file defines r as 'perintah' in [25] and then silently calls it 'peringkat' here and in [58], [59], [66]. The learner loses track that these are the same defined quantity.

examples.source: all elements $a \in \mathbb{Z}_n$ that are coprime with $N$
examples.translation: semua elemen ... yang koprosa dengan $N$
examples.suggested: yang koprima / perdana bersama dengan $N$
examples.why: 'Koprosa' is not a Malay word, and entry [59] uses 'koprim' for the same concept.

examples.source: the QFT converts this periodicity into measurable peaks
examples.translation: QFT menukar kekala ini kepada puncak yang boleh diukur
examples.suggested: QFT menukar keberkalaan ini kepada puncak yang boleh diukur
examples.why: 'Kekala' means permanence, the opposite idea to periodicity. This garbles the key intuition for why the QFT is used.

examples.source: Since some runs of the algorithm will statistically fail ... the results of the hardware run above
examples.translation: sesetengah jalankan algoritma ini ... keputusan jalankan perkakasan di atas
examples.suggested: sesetengah larian algoritma ini ... keputusan larian perkakasan di atas
examples.why: The imperative verb 'jalankan' is used where a noun is needed, so the sentence is ungrammatical. Entry [27] already uses 'larian' correctly.

examples.source: the presence of entanglement between the control and register qubits
examples.translation: kehadiran keterjalin antara qubit kawalan dan daftar
examples.suggested: kehadiran keterjalinan antara qubit kawalan dan qubit daftar
examples.why: 'Keterjalin' is a truncated form. The standard noun is 'keterjalinan'.

editor_note: "Commit" (inserting a check into the circuit for good) is translated with "mengesahkan/sahkan" ("verify/confirm") in [17], [57], [66] and [76]. The file also uses "sah" for *valid*, so a learner is taught that checks get validated rather than fixed into the circuit. The advice in [76] then reads as "validate fewer checks" instead of "add fewer checks", which is a FAIL. "Infers" is rendered as "mengekstrapolasikan" ("extrapolates") in [50] and [70]. "Draw a random sample" becomes "lukis sampel rawak" ("draw a picture of a sample") in [56]. Terminology also switches partway through the file: fidelity is fideliti/kesetiaan, stabilizer is penstabil/stabilizer, postselection is pemilihan-pasca/pascapilihan, and spacetime is ruang-masa/spacetime. "Entangling gates" becomes "get pengikat" ("binding gates") even though [14] correctly uses "dikusutkan".

examples.source: To raise the postselection rate, reduce the circuit depth or commit fewer checks
examples.translation: Untuk meningkatkan kadar pascapilihan, kurangkan kedalaman litar atau sahkan lebih sedikit pemeriksaan
examples.suggested: ... kurangkan kedalaman litar atau masukkan (tetapkan) lebih sedikit pemeriksaan
examples.why: 'sahkan' means validate/confirm, so the advice reads as 'validate fewer checks', not 'insert fewer checks'.

examples.source: checks are committed sequentially in the order the target qubits are given, and a committed check is not changed
examples.translation: pemeriksaan disahkan secara berurutan ... dan pemeriksaan yang telah disahkan tidak berubah
examples.suggested: pemeriksaan dimasukkan secara berurutan ... dan pemeriksaan yang telah dimasukkan tidak diubah
examples.why: This turns sequential insertion into sequential verification, and clashes with 'sah' = valid from [17].

examples.source: commits the best ones to the circuit ... when it uses few entangling gates
examples.translation: mengesahkan yang terbaik ke dalam litar ... menggunakan sedikit get pengikat
examples.suggested: memasukkan yang terbaik ke dalam litar ... menggunakan sedikit get pengusutan
examples.why: 'mengesahkan' is wrong for 'commit'. 'get pengikat' (binding gate) is not the entangling-gate term, and [14] already uses 'dikusutkan'.

examples.source: The model that follows infers a uniform depolarizing channel ... from benchmark data
examples.translation: Model yang berikut mengekstrapolasikan saluran depolarisasi seragam ...
examples.suggested: Model yang berikut menyimpulkan saluran depolarisasi seragam ...
examples.why: 'Extrapolate' is a different operation from 'infer'. The same error appears again in [70].

examples.source: Build the deeper circuit and draw a random sample of its stabilizers.
examples.translation: Bina litar yang lebih dalam dan lukis sampel rawak stabilizernya.
examples.suggested: Bina litar yang lebih dalam dan ambil sampel rawak stabilizernya.
examples.why: 'lukis' means draw as in plotting a picture. This is a calque of the sampling sense of 'draw'.

examples.source: Estimate fidelity from stabilizer sampling
examples.translation: Anggarkan kesetiaan daripada pensampelan stabilizer
examples.suggested: Anggarkan fideliti daripada pensampelan penstabil
examples.why: Entries [0]-[9] use 'fideliti' and 'penstabil', and from here on the file switches to 'kesetiaan' and 'stabilizer'.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through. The long caveat on diagonal-term filtering in [59], the pruning trade-off in [91] and the subspace-cost argument in [87] all keep their conditions and emphasis. The problems are inconsistent terms. "Ground state" is "keadaan dasar" in [0]/[1]/[9]/[30] but "keadaan asas" in [43]/[82]/[83]. Hamiltonian "terms" is "terma" in [20]-[28] but "sebutan" from [48] on. "Diagonalization" is "Diagonalisasi" in [13]/[14] but "pepenjuruan" in [59]/[82]/[96]. "Bitstring" is "bitstring" in [16]/[30] but "string bit" from [81] on. "Transpiler pass" is "pass" in [17] but "laluan" everywhere else. "Let the Hamiltonian be" in [18] is calqued as "Biarkan Hamiltonian".

examples.source: for the problem of ground state estimation
examples.translation: untuk masalah anggaran keadaan dasar
examples.suggested: untuk masalah anggaran keadaan asas (use one rendering throughout; [43]/[82]/[83] use 'keadaan asas')
examples.why: 'Ground state' is split between 'keadaan dasar' and 'keadaan asas' in the same file.

examples.source: Term grouping
examples.translation: Pengumpulan sebutan
examples.suggested: Keep 'sebutan' and change 'terma' in [20]-[28] to match (or the reverse)
examples.why: Hamiltonian 'terms' is 'terma' in the qDRIFT background section and 'sebutan' in the rest of the tutorial.

examples.source: Sample-based quantum diagonalization (SQD)
examples.translation: Diagonalisasi kuantum berasaskan sampel (SQD)
examples.suggested: Pepenjuruan kuantum berasaskan sampel (SQD)
examples.why: [96] and the body text use 'pepenjuruan' for the same concept, so the SQD/SKQD names are rendered two ways.

examples.source: fermionic layout and synthesis passes
examples.translation: pass susun atur dan sintesis fermionik
examples.suggested: laluan susun atur dan sintesis fermionik (match [47]/[71]/[73])
examples.why: 'Pass' is left in English here but rendered 'laluan' everywhere else.

examples.source: Let the Hamiltonian be of the form:
examples.translation: Biarkan Hamiltonian dalam bentuk:
examples.suggested: Andaikan Hamiltonian mempunyai bentuk:
examples.why: 'Biarkan' is a literal calque of the mathematical 'Let'. Malay technical writing uses 'Andaikan' or 'Katakan'.

editor_note: In entry [17], "correlators ⟨Z_i Z_j⟩" is translated as "pemerangkap", which means "trapper/catcher". A learner cannot recognise that as a correlation quantity and would be misled about what ⟨Z_i Z_j⟩ measures, so it should be "korelator" or "fungsi korelasi". "Observable(s)" is translated as "pemerhatian", which means "observation", in [17] and [51]. That mixes up the operator with the act of observing. Smaller naturalness slips: "menindih" for stacking Trotter steps [40], "Proses selepas" for post-process [52], "mencocoki" [53], and a switch from "kami" in [7] to "kita" everywhere else.

examples.source: more reliable estimates of spin observables like $\langle Z_i \rangle$ and correlators $\langle Z_i Z_j \rangle$
examples.translation: anggaran yang lebih dipercayai bagi pemerhatian spin seperti $\langle Z_i \rangle$ dan pemerangkap $\langle Z_i Z_j \rangle$
examples.suggested: anggaran yang lebih dipercayai bagi boleh cerap spin seperti $\langle Z_i \rangle$ dan korelator $\langle Z_i Z_j \rangle$
examples.why: 'pemerangkap' means trapper/catcher, so it teaches a false concept for a correlation function. 'pemerhatian' means observation, not observable.

examples.source: each item contains a circuit and the corresponding Pauli-Z observables
examples.translation: setiap item mengandungi Circuit dan pemerhatian Pauli-Z yang sepadan
examples.suggested: setiap item mengandungi litar dan boleh cerap Pauli-Z yang sepadan
examples.why: 'pemerhatian' (observation) mixes up the measured operator with the act of observing.

examples.source: By stacking multiple Trotter steps
examples.translation: Dengan menindih beberapa langkah Trotter
examples.suggested: Dengan menyusun beberapa langkah Trotter secara berturutan
examples.why: 'menindih' suggests pressing down or overlapping, not stacking layers in sequence.

examples.source: Step 4: Post-process and return result in desired classical format
examples.translation: Langkah 4: Proses selepas dan kembalikan keputusan dalam format klasik yang diingini
examples.suggested: Langkah 4: Pasca-proses dan kembalikan keputusan dalam format klasik yang diingini
examples.why: 'Proses selepas' is a word-for-word copy of the English that no native technical writer would use.

examples.source: shows how closely the hardware execution with Fire Opal matches the noiseless baseline
examples.translation: menunjukkan betapa rapatnya pelaksanaan perkakasan dengan Fire Opal mencocoki garis dasar tanpa hingar
examples.suggested: menunjukkan sejauh mana pelaksanaan perkakasan dengan Fire Opal sepadan dengan garis dasar tanpa hingar
examples.why: 'mencocoki' is an uncommon, stiff word choice; 'sepadan dengan' is the natural phrasing.
